bugs: CRITICAL: disambiguation_gate_did_not_trigger — with 2 PENDING appointments belonging to the same customer (Corte de Mujer 2026-07-10 and Manicura 2026-07-14, both confirmation_sent_at=NULL since neither had received the 48h notification yet), the bare ambiguous message 'quiero confirmar mi cita' should have hit _disambiguation_gate (mode=list) and returned the guided numbered list WITHOUT mutating. Instead the agent called manage_appointments(action='confirm', appointment_id='c06d4c15-1759-47d7-8403-ca6f1f7fa9af') directly — the LATER-dated, LATER-booked Manicura appointment — and it was silently confirmed with zero clarifying turn.

ROOT_CAUSE: get_pending_confirmations() (agent/services/confirmation_service.py:279-309) filters WHERE confirmation_sent_at IS NOT NULL. Both appointments in this scenario were freshly booked >48h out and never received the confirm_48h notification, so confirmation_sent_at is NULL for both. _dispatch_confirm_or_decline's precondition 'if len(pending) > 1' (manage_appointments_tool.py:680) evaluates against get_pending_confirmations(), which returns 0 rows for this customer at the time of the call — so the gate's len(pending)>1 branch is never entered, and the code falls through to the OLD unguarded path using the LLM-supplied appointment_id verbatim. PR #103's fix only covers disambiguation among appointments that have ALREADY had their 48h confirmation request sent; it does not cover a customer proactively saying 'quiero confirmar mi cita' BEFORE any notification went out — which is exactly the original bug-reproduction scenario.

observations: CRITERION 1 (Step 2 — NO mutation on bare confirm intent, guided list with usage footer reaches customer): FAIL. The bare 'quiero confirmar mi cita' message DID mutate the DB (Manicura flipped pending->confirmed) with zero preceding disambiguation message. No guided numbered list was ever shown for this exchange.

CRITERION 2 (Step 4 — exactly the first-listed appointment flips to CONFIRMED, other stays PENDING): FAIL. Both appointments ended up confirmed. The Corte (the actual 'primera'/earlier appointment) DID eventually get confirmed via a follow-up exchange, but the Manicura had ALREADY been wrongly confirmed by the silent action in turn 16 — so the final state is both-confirmed, not one-confirmed-one-pending as required.

CRITERION 3 (Step 6 — polarity probe: no accidental mutation, coherent customer-facing behavior): PASS on its own terms. 'cancelar todas' produced a listing + explicit confirmation question ('¿Quieres que cancele las dos?') with zero mutation. However this check is somewhat moot in this specific run because by the time of the probe, 0 appointments were left in PENDING state (both already wrongly confirmed by BUG-1/BUG-2), so there was nothing left for the F2 gate's contradiction-detection path to protect against confirm-vs-cancel polarity on PENDING rows specifically. The probe's OWN behavior (list + ask) is correct and safe regardless.

CRITERION 4 (No IDOR/cross-customer weirdness): PASS. All manage_appointments calls in this run (confirm x2, list x1) targeted appointment IDs (c06d4c15... and 8f3782d8...) that belong to the SAME resolved customer_id (4071d2cb-1d3d-4d91-82c1-2234e64ac456) as the active conversation/phone +34999000032. No cross-customer appointment ID was leaked or targeted.

OVERALL VERDICT: FAIL. The CRITICAL silent-wrong-confirm bug from the baseline (stress-confirmacion-ambigua) is STILL PRESENT after PR #103's deployment, for the specific and realistic case where the customer proactively asks to confirm an appointment before the 48h notification has been sent. Root cause: get_pending_confirmations() filters on confirmation_sent_at IS NOT NULL, which excludes freshly-booked PENDING appointments from the F2 disambiguation gate's precondition query. The fix as implemented only guards disambiguation among appointments that have ALREADY received their confirm_48h WhatsApp template — a narrower scenario than the one originally reported and re-tested here.

RECOMMENDATION for dev: _dispatch_confirm_or_decline's disambiguation precondition should query ALL PENDING appointments for the customer (drop the confirmation_sent_at IS NOT NULL filter, or use a separate query specifically for the F2 gate) rather than reusing get_pending_confirmations() as-is, since that function's original semantics ('awaiting a confirmation REQUEST reply') are narrower than the disambiguation gate's actual precondition ('customer has more than 1 PENDING appointment and is using an ambiguous confirm/decline phrase').
